result.title: How Efficient Is Your Agent? Online Predictive Bounds under Budget Constraints
result.summary: We evaluate AI agents in an online setting where tasks arrive sequentially and, before running each task, we construct an upper predictive bound on its \emph{time-to-success}---the number of interactions until the task is completed successfully. Under a limited budget, some runs are stopped early, so their time-to-success is unobserved (right-censored), and the correctness of the bound may be unknown. We introduce \emph{\textbf{PR}edictive Bounds for \textbf{O}nline \textbf{B}udget \textbf{E}fficiency} (\texttt{PROBE}), a method for constructing calibrated upper predictive bounds while adaptively allocating a limited budget across agent tasks to reduce the anticipated coverage deficit. Our method calibrates the bounds online using inverse-probability-weighted feedback together with a correction designed to minimize coverage deficit while remaining unbiased. We prove that \texttt{PROBE} provides a coverage guarantee for any finite time horizon while satisfying the budget constraint. Experiments on software engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and instruction following show that \texttt{PROBE} attains a coverage rate closer to the target level with tighter predictive bounds than a calibrated baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PROBE：在任务顺序到达、预算有限且部分运行因提前停止导致 time-to-success 右删失的情况下，在线构建经过校准的成功时间上界预测，并自适应地在任务间分配预算以降低覆盖缺口，同时给出有限时域下的覆盖保证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「预算约束下右删失反馈＋在线校准上界」的统计框架可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策与动态计算成本的评价提供可借用的度量工具，但论文对象是 agent 级效率而非推理内部状态，与视觉证据或 latent 表示无直接关联，可迁移性需核查。
